A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same COD research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantive revisions.

before.justification: v3 reports original prediction experiments for 70B and 12B models, clustering and mapping ablations, and continued-pretraining results.

after.justification: v4 reports original 70B prediction results, ablations, continued-pretraining results, and a new dense-to-MoE transfer experiment.

M1.justification: Appendix A.1 replaces the fixed clustering radius with an estimated bandwidth capped by a distance-based upper bound. Section 4.4 replaces quartic-polynomial mapping with a cubic smoothing spline whose complexity is adjusted to meet an RMSE threshold. Both changes alter the prediction procedure.

E1.justification: The eight downstream benchmarks, CEval pilot, multilingual training domains, and continued-pretraining coverage remain. Adding a MoE target and removing the 12B prediction experiment change model configurations rather than the represented data or task requirements.

E2.justification: The four main baselines remain, with standardized names. Appendix C.3 adds anchor-assisted exponential and BNSL comparisons and removes the in-domain-anchor COD variant. The alternative spline and polynomial comparison in v3 Appendix C.2 is also removed.

E3.justification: v4 adds one-shot evaluation of a 32B activated-parameter MoE target using dense-model clusters, while removing the 12B-target protocol using 122M–1.9B sources. The main COD results switch from the in-domain-anchor configuration to Qwen2-72B anchoring, and new baseline controls receive the same anchor. These materially revise the evaluation design.

E4.justification: v4 adds architecture-transfer testing, replaces the mapping-family ablation with spline RMSE-threshold sensitivity, and expands anchor analysis with baseline controls and MATH/MMLU-pro case plots. It removes the quantitative 12B scale analysis and in-domain-versus-out-of-domain anchor comparison. Clustering, extrapolation-formula, and filtering-threshold analyses remain with revised results.

E5.justification: Both versions retain 100-sample pass-rate estimation and averaging across three adjacent checkpoints. Neither adds seed information, independent-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests; the new MoE experiment does not introduce an uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces COD's mean/maximum errors of 1.63%/2.38% with 1.55%/2.68% under the revised method and anchoring configuration. Continued-pretraining mean error changes from 2.33% to 2.18%, and numerous ablation values change. v4 adds MoE results of 3.11% mean and 8.11% maximum error, anchor-assisted baseline results, and target/anchor scores, while deleting the 12B results.

T1.justification: Theorem 1, its three assumptions, the arithmetic–geometric mean lemma, and Appendix B's proof remain unchanged. The limited formal change is removal of the explicitly defined endpoint-constrained polynomial mapping family in v3 Eq. (5) when v4 adopts spline mapping.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction revise the headline average prediction error from 1.36% to 1.55%; v3's Table 1 instead reported 1.63%. The central contributions—difficulty clustering, cluster-wise scaling, and subset-to-full prediction—retain their meaning and scope.

C2.justification: v4 adds a hyperparameter/deployment limitation and expands v3's small-source warning into a stronger small-target limitation, including a claimed advantage for PassUntil. MoE discussion changes from expected architectural invariance to qualified interpretation of measured transfer. Mapping and anchor explanations are substantially revised, including a new claim of no baseline benefit that Table A3 does not support for BNSL.

D1.justification: v4 specifies sklearn's bandwidth estimator, Q=0.1, the radius cap, and spline fitting with RMSE threshold 0.005. It explains how anchors enter baseline fitting and explicitly excludes target-model evaluations from difficulty features. Appendix D's dense-model architectures, training recipe, hardware information, and software disclosures remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds discussion and citations for Ruan et al., Ye et al., and Bhagia et al., and removes the GShard citation associated with the deleted in-domain anchor. It distinguishes exponential from piecewise prediction methods and expands positioning against Hu et al.; the main research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: v4 adds an introductory mechanism explanation, refines method prose, restructures the end-to-end related-work discussion, standardizes baseline names, and changes CPT terminology to CT. The overall narrative and section hierarchy remain recognizable, with local subsection changes and appendix renumbering after removal of the 12B study.

P2.justification: The document changes from the branded report layout to ICLR formatting, including typography, title/abstract treatment, headers, and references. Figure 2 is redrawn, mapping displays are replaced and expanded, and MoE and anchor-score tables are added. The difficulty-distribution figure is retained and renumbered, while the 12B table disappears.

improvement.justification: v4 adds useful implementation detail, shared-anchor baseline controls, empirical MoE evidence, and a consistent headline error. However, it removes the quantitative 12B study and introduces misleading interpretation: Appendix C.3 claims baselines gain no anchor benefit although BNSL's mean error falls from 5.17% to 3.60%. The new MoE table also reports a loss-intermediate mean of 3.65%, whereas its seven listed errors average about 3.23%. These benefits and losses leave the net quality direction uncertain.
